proof_attempt_summary: The run attempted an endpoint-preserving reduction from finite selection-aware σ-MAGs to ordinary MAGs, followed by transfer of Zhang's completed-PAG orientation theorem and finite opposing realizers. The proof audit found that `lem:directed-anterior-compression` did not justify collapsing undirected component segments across normalized exits and re-entries; consequently, normalization ancestrality/maximality and every downstream completeness claim remain unverified. A componentwise or quotient-acyclic collapse argument may repair a coherent subfield theorem, but the cold panel found no bounded route from that repair to the field floor.
tldr: Can every finite selection-aware \(\sigma\)-MAG be converted, by consistently ordering only those undirected components that receive arrowheads, into a separation-equivalent ordinary MAG while preserving any requested tail endpoint? The proposal advances the affirmative answer as a precise theorem to audit. If its maximality lemma survives, every nonempty \(\sigma\)-fiber lies in the nonempty ordinary-fiber domain of the partial completed-endpoint map, ordinary and \(\sigma\)-MAG members realize exactly the same endpoint marks, and Zhang's completed-PAG rules \(R0\)--\(R10\) become sound and complete under an explicit maintained selection-aware \(\sigma\)-faithfulness premise, with opposite-mark representatives for every residual circle.
gap: Yao--Mooij supply the first unrestricted selection-aware \(\sigma\)-MAG semantics and equivalence criterion but explicitly leave complete FCI open. Zhang supplies complete ordinary PAG orientation with selection, while Mooij--Claassen supply the cyclic transfer only after excluding selection. The missing fact is not another local rule: it is whether every \(\sigma\)-class has sufficiently endpoint-flexible ordinary representatives.
fill: Prove or refute the ordered-component normal form, with maximality as the primary obligation. On the affirmative branch, prove coordinatewise equality of endpoint-mark sets, instantiate Zhang's source-faithful rule schedule including \(R5\)--\(R7\), and return finite opposing representatives for every circle. On the negative branch, exhibit and verify a smallest counterexample and characterize the boundary on which normalization succeeds.
